issues.description: Command names don't match existing convention (quickmark_save vs quickmarks_reload).
issues.detail: The file already has quickmark_save, quickmark_add, quickmark_load (singular, registered as :quickmark-save etc). This patch introduces quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload (plural). Match the surrounding code's voice: quickmark_reload, bookmark_reload. The feature tests then need :quickmark-reload, :bookmark-reload. Inconsistency in command naming is exactly the kind of papercut a maintainer regrets six years later.

issues.description: Reload reads the file before save-manager is wired on first construction.
issues.detail: __init__ now calls self.reload() before _init_savemanager(). reload() emits self.changed, which in the original __init__ path was deliberately avoided during construction (the old code did not emit changed on initial load). If anything is connected to changed before _init_savemanager runs, fine; but the emit-on-initial-load is a behavior change snuck in alongside a refactor. Split it, or suppress the signal on initial load.

issues.description: Two unrelated commands in one patch; should be two.
issues.detail: quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload are two separate user-facing features that happen to share a base class change. Land the urlmarks.reload() refactor as patch one, quickmark-reload command as patch two, bookmark-reload command as patch three. When this regresses, bisect should land on a commit that does one thing. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Feature test scenarios are missing titles.
issues.detail: Every other Scenario in urlmarks.feature has a descriptive name (Scenario: Saving a quickmark). The two new scenarios are anonymous (Scenario:). Name them: 'Scenario: Reloading bookmarks' and 'Scenario: Reloading quickmarks'. Match the file's voice.

issues.description: Unit test doesn't verify clear-then-load semantics; only the happy replacement case.
issues.detail: test_reload writes one entry, constructs, overwrites the file, calls reload. It doesn't test that an entry present in memory but removed from disk actually disappears, nor that adding a second entry on disk yields two entries. The clear() in reload() is load-bearing and unverified. One more assertion catches the obvious regression.

issues.description: Stray blank line and dead method shape in __init__.
issues.detail: The new __init__ has `self.reload()` followed by a blank line then `self._init_savemanager(...)`. Minor, but the original block was tight. Also: the reload() method now duplicates the exact loop the constructor used to inline; that's fine and correct, just confirm no other caller still expects the old non-clearing initial-load behavior.

review.summary: Small, mostly sensible patch: factor the file-load loop into reload(), expose it as a command. The shape is right. Three things bug me. One: naming inconsistency — every existing command here is :quickmark-* / :bookmark- (singular), and this patch ships :quickmarks-reload / :bookmarks-reload. Match the codebase's voice. Two: this is really three patches glued together (refactor + two commands) and should be split for bisectability. Three: reload() now emits changed on initial construction where the old code didn't, which is a behavior change hiding in a refactor. NEEDS-WORK — fix the names, split the patch, and decide deliberately about the initial-load signal.
